To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we developed a Bayesian version of GPFA that scales near linearly in time and can incorporate non-Gaussian noise, (ii) we applied bGPFA to 30 minutes of continuous neural activity, revealing that preparatory latent dynamics are predictive of behavioral reaction times, and (iii) we discovered slow latent processes with behavioral relevance

(1) bGPFA is a scalable Bayesian GPFA method that can be used to discover latent processes that evolve on slow timescales and are predictive of reaction times; (2) bGPFA discovers preparatory dynamics that precede movement initiation; and (3) bGPFA can be applied to large continuous recordings without trial-structure.

we develop a fully Bayesian version of GPFA with automatic determination of the latent dimension, and that this method reveals preparatory dynamics in the motor system and slow timescale fluctuations in the somatosensory system.

developing scalable methods for latent variable models that can be applied to large-scale datasets.
the development of scalable, flexible and principled methods for the analysis of high-dimensional neural recordings.
developing scalable, flexible methods for latent variable models that allow for the analysis of neural population data in a principled manner.

the present study introduces a scalable Bayesian method for latent variable modeling of continuous neural recordings, and that this method can be successfully used to uncover latent processes that are relevant for the behavior of interest.
the bGPFA model provides a flexible, scalable, and principled approach for analyzing neural population data.
bGPFA is a powerful and scalable Bayesian method that can be used for the analysis of large-scale neural population recordings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new scalable Bayesian GPFA model with discrete noise models and automatic relevance determination.

we develop an efficient, scalable, flexible, and fully Bayesian version of Gaussian process latent variable models that allows for a principled and interpretable analysis of neural population activity.

we developed a scalable Bayesian GPFA model that is applicable to continuous neural recordings, and we demonstrated its use on continuous recordings spanning 14 million data-points from a reaching task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of flexible priors and scalable inference allows for the analysis of continuous neural recordings at a level of detail previously possible only in the low data regime.
scalable Bayesian methods are now feasible for the analysis of large neural datasets and that they can be used to discover latent dynamics at a range of timescales.
bGPFA is able to scale to large datasets while still providing a principled and flexible framework for the analysis of neural population data.
